001: Ivan, how have your first few weeks been with our team? Have you managed to get into the work rhythm?
Honestly, at first it wasn't easy getting used to such a pace, but my colleagues helped a lot.
It's great that you're not afraid to ask questions. That's always welcome here.
I noticed that you have a habit of openly discussing mistakes, and that surprised me a bit.
Yes, we believe it's better to identify a problem right away than to spend a long time fixing the consequences later.
I agree, this approach really helps you learn faster and not repeat the same mistakes.
002: Dmitry, have you gotten used to our weekly meetings yet, or do they still seem too long?
To be honest, at first they seemed drawn out to me, but now I see that they're useful for keeping everyone on the same page.
We try to make them as productive as possible so we don't waste the team's time.
I like that everyone has the right to speak up and offer their own idea.
That's the foundation of our culture — we value initiative and aren't afraid to discuss different points of view.
Great, then next time I'll prepare a few suggestions for our project too.
003: Sergey, how do you feel in the informal setting after work? Are you comfortable?
I'll admit, I was a bit surprised that you're used to socializing outside the office so often.
For us, it's a way to get to know each other better and strengthen team spirit.
I understand, it helps you trust each other in work matters too.
Exactly. When you know a person better, it's easier to find common ground in difficult situations.
I suppose you're right. I'm starting to appreciate this approach, even though it was unusual at first.
004: Anna, tell me, how did you adapt to our rule of planning your own day?
At first it was unusual, since before I was used to stricter control from management.
We deliberately give employees freedom so they feel responsible for the results.
Now I understand that it develops discipline and the ability to set priorities.
And, by the way, you're doing a great job — your last report was very well structured.
Thank you, it's nice to hear that. I'll try to keep living up to your trust.
005: Ivan, how do you feel about our custom of giving feedback right after a presentation?
Honestly, at first it wasn't easy, but I see huge value in it for growth.
We try to do it constructively so that everyone can improve their work.
Yes, your comments are always specific and about the substance, not the person.
That's an important principle — we criticize the idea, not the person who suggested it.
That's exactly why I feel at ease and am ready to openly discuss my shortcomings.
006: Elena, have you gotten used to the fact that we often make decisions collectively?
At first it seemed to me that it slowed things down, but now I see that it reduces risks.
We believe that collective discussion allows us to take all the nuances into account and avoid mistakes.
I agree, especially when it comes to complex tasks where every detail matters.
And besides, when everyone takes part in the decision, everyone feels responsible for carrying it out.
Yes, that really increases the engagement and motivation of the whole team.
007: Dmitry, how did you take to our tradition of celebrating project successes at the end of each stage?
I'll admit, at first I thought it was unnecessary, but then I realized it's great motivation.
We believe it's important to acknowledge achievements, not just work on mistakes.
It helps the team feel that their work is valued and gives them energy for the future.
Besides, new ideas often come up in an informal setting, and bonds get stronger.
I agree, now I look forward to those gatherings and even suggest reasons for them myself.
008: Olga, how did you adapt to our principle of transparency in communication between departments?
At first I was surprised that we could directly discuss things with other teams without intermediaries.
We removed unnecessary barriers to speed up the exchange of information and decision-making.
It really saves time and lets us solve problems faster.
And, importantly, it reduces the number of misunderstandings and conflicts.
I completely agree with you, this approach makes the work much more efficient.
009: Sergey, how do you feel about our rule of not working overtime unless it's absolutely necessary?
Honestly, I was pleasantly surprised, because before I often stayed late at work.
We believe that overworking lowers productivity and leads to burnout.
You're right, taking care of the work-life balance is really important for long-term effectiveness.
That's why we try to plan the workload so that everything gets done during work hours.
That's a very wise approach, and I can see that the team works smoothly and without unnecessary stress.
010: Anna, how are you getting used to our style of communication with management? Does it seem open enough to you?
Yes, it was a pleasant discovery for me that you can calmly discuss ideas with the director.
We try to support horizontal connections and remove excessive hierarchy.
It helps you feel like part of one team, not just someone carrying out orders.
Exactly, we want every employee to feel that their opinion matters.
Thank you for that attitude, it really inspires me to work better and suggest new things.
